entrypoints.summary: SubmissionFromBinding and SubmissionToBinding accept or emit validator-address/signature tuples at the Go/Solidity binding conversion boundary.
SubmissionToBinding sorts signatures by claimed ValidatorAddress and serializes each claimed address with its supplied signature into bindings.ValidatorSigTuple.

affected_components.role: Copies validator-address/signature pairs across Go and Solidity binding representations; SubmissionToBinding sorts by claimed validator address.

code_slices.fixed: The PR excerpt invokes k1util.Verify with sigTup.ValidatorAddress, attRoot, and sigTup.Signature, returns an invalid-attestation-signature error on false verification, and rejects duplicate validator signatures.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The supplied abi.go source is a current project context revision and is not established as the audited vulnerable revision.
code_slices.vulnerable: The report excerpts both conversion functions copying ValidatorAddress/ValidatorAddr and Signature without signature verification; the provided Go source also shows SubmissionToBinding sorting by ValidatorAddress before serializing tuples.

sources.concept: validator-address/signature tuple at ABI conversion boundary

impact.affected_asset: Integrity of validator identity attribution in xchain submission signature tuples.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause a mismatched claimed-validator-address/signature tuple to be represented and, in the submission-to-binding path, deterministically ordered by the claimed address before this conversion layer rejects it. No downstream unauthorized execution is established.
impact.security_effect: Low-severity validator signature identity-integrity failure at an off-chain ABI conversion boundary; on-chain signature verification is documented as a mitigating condition.

causal_trace.summary: A submission tuple contains a claimed validator address and a signature supplied together at the binding/submission conversion boundary.
The conversion path constructs corresponding tuple representations without first establishing that the claimed validator address is the signer authenticated by the signature.

SubmissionToBinding orders tuples by the unverified claimed validator address and copies that address and signature into bindings.ValidatorSigTuple; the reverse conversion similarly copies the pair into SigTuple.

This creates an unverified validator-identity/signature representation that can be ordered or consumed as if bound. The audit states OmniPortal.sol verifies signatures on-chain, so the demonstrated impact is limited to this local representation-integrity gap rather than a shown authorization bypass.

failure.operation: Constructing, sorting, and serializing validator-address/signature tuples before cryptographically binding the supplied signature to the claimed validator address.

primary_invariant.statement: Every validator address carried in a submission signature tuple must be cryptographically verified as the identity that signed the applicable attestation data before the tuple is converted, ordered, or relied upon.
primary_invariant.violated_because: Both conversion functions copy the claimed address and signature between SigTuple and bindings.ValidatorSigTuple without address-against-signature verification; one path also sorts by the claimed address.

quality.review_notes: The audit report directly identifies the conversion functions, missing address/signature verification, low rating, on-chain OmniPortal verification, recommendation, and PR #2137 resolution. The supplied source slice confirms address-based sorting and tuple serialization but is explicitly not proven to be the audited pre-fix revision. The PR excerpt confirms verifier rejection logic, but no complete patch diff, regression test, test execution, or consumer trace is present. Accordingly, no unauthorized execution, successful exploit, or reproducible behavior is asserted.

remediation.invariant_restored: Verify each signature against the claimed validator address and attestation root before accepting the tuple, rejecting invalid signatures and duplicate validator addresses.
